newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Sri Lanka leads as week ends.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Sri Lanka leads as week ends.

text.p: Asian debt markets finished the week off slowly, offering just a couple of new issues.
Sri Lanka launched its US$50 million floating rate issue during London hours overnight. The notes mature in five years but can be put after two.
They float at 150 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate and pay combined fees of 100 basis points.
Citicorp International and ING Barings were the leads.
Sri Lanka is tapping the international capital markets after a 15-year absence in order to create a benchmark for other Sri Lankan borrowers.

Proceeds of the FRN will be used to supplement loans from multilateral agencies for use in developing the country's infrastructure, Sri Lanka's central bank governor A.S. Jayawardena said during the roadshow for the notes.
Also overnight, Indonesia's PT Ongko launched and priced a US$100 million seven-year bond.
The 10.50 percent bond was priced and re-offered at 99.4642 to yield 400 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
Closing out a banner week for the Philippines was news that yet another supranational agency plans to launch a peso-denominated Eurobond.
Manila has approved a proposal from the The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to issue one-year Europeso notes worth 3.0 billion pesos.
The World Bank and the International Finance Corp brought peso Eurobonds to global markets for the first time in two separate issues this week.
In a related development, the Philippine peso has been accepted as a settlement currency in the Euroclear system.
Euroclear said the move reflects its commitment to expanding its network to emerging markets. It now clears transactions in 37 currencies.
In the loan market, Asia Terminals Ltd has mandated ABN Amro and Societe Generale Asia to arrange a HK$1.75 billion loan, the arrangers said.

Bankers said Hong Kong blue chip company Sun Hung Kai Properties is pondering a loan of at least HK$5.0 billion in size. SHK Properties is expected to lead the loan itself with the aid of an arranger group.
The facility is expected to be five to seven years in tenor.
South Korea announced today that it had repealed limits on the amount in loans that Korea local banks can borrow overseas.
